evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Nicole says 'This call will just take around five to ten minutes then I will be able to build you an accurate code. You can depend on, sounds good.' — timeboxed and promise made, but no clear wait for a yes before moving into probing.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Nicole asks: 'I'd like to ask first what are your biggest concerns and what are the most important things you want answers to on this call today aside from the code.' — asked early, before logistics probing starts.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises concern about furniture handling (couches, coffee table, expensive items, prior bad experience). Nicole follows up: 'Will there be anything, aside from the couch? Will there be anything heavy like, art? I mean, workout equipment, safe panel.' Then digs deeper into weight/specifics and takes notes. On TV sizes: 'Oh, okay. Good to hear that. Are they a big TV like more than sixty inches?' Continues probing into specifics.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Nicole acknowledges concerns multiple times ('Mm-hmm', 'I see', 'No worries. I'll take note of that') and mentions taking notes, but does not deliver a structured summary reflection like 'So what I'm hearing is X, Y, and Z. Did I get all of it?'
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Covered: property type (apartment, then house), floor/stories (2nd floor with elevator; destination 1-story), rooms (3-bed but 2-bed + study), walking distance (two school buses from curb to elevator at origin; 5 steps at door to elevator), parking (street parking at destination), special considerations (furniture protection needs, TVs), appliances (washer/dryer, two TVs). Destination address initially auto-populated incorrectly, then manually corrected to 1262 Hethwood Court, Haslet 76052.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Nicole asks: 'For a typical three bedroom apartment we usually expect to see around $35 to 45 box system move. Do you think you'll follow within that range?' Customer responds under 20 boxes. Later Nicole confirms TV packing in boxes.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Not offered. Nicole does not ask 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Nicole says: 'We charge $222 per hour for two movers and one truck' and later 'we charge $222 per hour for two movers and one truck. And we provide 26 foot box truck with everything needed.' Personalized to this move: mentions the travel fee ($115 one-time), wrap and pads included, notes furniture protection for their specific concerns (couches, TVs). Full anchor with personalization.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Nicole discloses: '$222 per hour... everything is included in this hourly rate like fuel and truck taxes, insurance, all wrap pads and bans... There's only wanting outside of the hourly rate, which is the one time travel fee of $115... There's no hidden fees of any type. No credit card fees, no disassemble or reassembly fees. No sterle fees.' Fee transparency upfront. She also says 'we charge $222 per hour' and explains inclusions clearly. However, the '2.5-hour-minimum / 15-minute-increments commitment framing' is not explicitly stated. Partial — fee transparency present, minimum/increment commitment not stated.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. The call moves directly into Section 5 (Two Promises) without asking 'Does that feel fair?' or pausing for customer reaction to pricing.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Nicole begins: 'Finally ally, we have on time guarantee if we cannot make it in the time window that we arrange, we immediately...' — then the line cuts off due to audio breakup. The sentence is incomplete; the discount terms (starts discounting immediately if late) are not fully delivered. Partial — mentioned but not fully explained.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Nicole states: 'We have no worries damage coverage we provide up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for any accidental damages.' Covers $2,000 and repair/replace/reimburse but does not explicitly state 'no deductible' or 'no fine print' framing, nor that it is built into the rate (not an add-on). Partial — the $2,000 and coverage type are clear, but the no-deductible and built-in framing are missing.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Nicole does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent. Call cuts off mid-Two Promises delivery (audio breakup on On-Time Guarantee).
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. The call ends during Section 5 delivery; Section 6 (Concerns Again) with 'What's still concerning you about this move?' is never reached.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Not asked. 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' is not asked.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked. The call drops before Section 7 (Ask for the Business). No version of 'Would you like our help with your move?' is spoken.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Not mentioned. Call ends before booking discussion.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Not confirmed. Call ends mid-Section 5; no booking details (date, phone, arrival window, crew size, addresses, notes) are confirmed.

top_strength: Nicole asked 'Their Agenda' before any logistics probing and then dug two layers deep into each concern the customer raised (furniture protection, prior bad experiences, furniture specifics), taking notes and showing genuine listening throughout.
coaching_note: The call ended abruptly during Section 5 (Two Promises) due to audio breakup, but more critically: never ask 'Does that feel fair?' after pricing, skip the 2.5-hour-minimum framing, never complete the On-Time Guarantee explanation, and never reach Sections 6 or 7 — establish the full sales sequence to close the loop and ask for the business before audio issues or time pressure interrupt the flow.
